subject.title: [Bug]: Slack reaction_added/reaction_removed events never delivered via Socket Mode (multi-account, v2026.3.24)

question: Should a fix PR wait for live current-main Slack Socket Mode reaction envelope proof before changing this path?
rationale: Source inspection proves OpenClaw has handler-level support, but only live diagnostics can identify whether this report fails before Bolt delivery, at the account/team filter, or later in authorization.

options.title: Require live envelope proof
options.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a redacted current-main multi-account Slack trace before accepting a code change.

options.title: Consolidate into broad Socket Mode triage
options.body: Close or duplicate this only after https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/89222 gains public diagnostics that preserve the reaction-specific failure.

options.title: Sponsor speculative diagnosis
options.body: A maintainer can explicitly own a live Slack investigation branch, accepting that the first PR may be diagnostic instrumentation rather than a product fix.

recommendation.title: Require live envelope proof
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and ask for a redacted current-main multi-account Slack trace before accepting a code change.

likelyOwner.reason: The closest merged routing fix and issue discussion for Slack reaction system events are tied to Vincent Koc's PR history.
